title: A smooth affine maximal graph in dimension ten
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's construction (2026) of a smooth function on R^10 with positive definite Hessian, not a quadratic polynomial, that solves the affine maximal equation, the Euler-Lagrange equation of the affine area. The course derives the equation from the affine area (Jacobi's formula and divergence-free cofactors of a Hessian); reduces it, for graphs u = sqrt(F(x)^2 + t^2), to two second-order equations for F and an auxiliary function P of one variable fewer, and for radial F and P to a system of ordinary differential equations; solves that system through the origin by the contraction mapping principle in the variable s = r^2/2; and shows, in the dimension m = 9, that three logarithmic derivatives stay in a box whose upper corner (9/2, 7/2, 33/7) comes from the singular example sqrt(|x|^9 + t^2) of Trudinger and Wang, so the solution exists for all radii.
prerequisites: real analysis in one and several variables: core courses Real Analysis I and II (Lebl, Basic Analysis I and II, version 6.3): the mean value theorem (Theorem 4.2.4), the fundamental theorem of calculus (Theorems 5.3.1 and 5.3.3), the change of variables (Theorem 5.3.5), completeness of C([a,b]) and of closed subsets (Propositions 7.4.5 and 7.4.6), extreme values and uniform continuity on compact sets (Theorems 7.5.6 and 7.5.11), continuity of parameter integrals (Proposition 7.5.12), the contraction mapping principle (Theorem 7.6.2), differentiation under the integral sign (Theorem 9.1.1), integrals of continuous functions over rectangles (Theorem 10.1.15) and Fubini's theorem (Theorem 10.2.2)
linear algebra: determinants, the Leibniz formula, symmetric matrices and their eigenvalues

checks.reading: The manuscript 'A Smooth Nonquadratic Entire Affine Maximal Graph in Dimension Ten' (OpenAI, 5 Oct 2026; build/source/main.tex, 481 lines, 18 kB of TeX; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: (1) the first lesson derives the affine maximal equation as the Euler-Lagrange equation of the affine area, with Jacobi's formula and the divergence-free rows of the cofactor matrix of a Hessian, where the manuscript cites Trudinger and Wang; (2) the facts on ordinary differential equations that the manuscript uses as standard (local existence and uniqueness for systems, maximal solutions, continuation from a compact set) are proved in the fourth lesson from the contraction mapping principle; (3) the invariance of the box is shown with explicit formulas for the field on the upper faces, where the manuscript compares with the stationary corner through the signs of the cross derivatives, and the exit argument is written out with a first exit time; (4) Remark 2.2 of the second lesson records the converse of the reduction. Attributions checked: Trudinger and Wang, Invent. Math. 140 (2000), introduction and Section 7 (the singular example sqrt(|x|^9 + x_10^2)), on Wang's ANU page. Field state on 17 Oct 2026: a lecture announcement of X.-J. Wang (SCMS Gu Lecture, Fudan University, 29 Apr 2026) states a counterexample to the affine Bernstein problem in dimensions ten and higher, without describing its regularity; no written version was found.
